 Only 2,663 Estates Owed Federal Estate Tax in Returns Filed in 2024. The Biggest 469 Paid Most of the Bill
 David Beren Sat, November 14, 2026 at 12:16 PM CST 5 min read Quick Read 
 Federal estate tax hits very few families: just 2,663 of 7,195 estate returns filed in 2024 owed tax, totaling about $23 billion. 
 Estates worth $50 million or more paid about 68% of all net estate tax while making up only 18% of taxpaying estates. 
 The exemption now stands at $15 million per person in 2026, up from $13.61 million in 2024, shielding couples up to $30 million.

 In 2024, only 2,663 estates owed federal estate tax, according to IRS Statistics of Income. They accounted for 7,195 estate tax returns filed that year, and together they paid $23,313,220,000. Plenty of families spend years worrying about the "death tax." In practice, it falls on a very small group, and most of the money comes from an even smaller group at the top. 
 utah778 / Getty Images Three terms help explain the IRS data that follows. The gross estate is everything a person owned when they died: the house, brokerage accounts, retirement accounts, business interests, even art. The taxable estate is what's left after deductions, such as property going to a spouse or a charity. The exemption, which the tax code calls the basic exclusion amount, is the part of an estate the federal government doesn't tax. Only the value above it is taxable.

 How 469 Estates Covered Most of the Bill 
 Estates worth $50 million or more paid about 68% of all net estate tax on 2024 returns. Yet they made up only about 18% of the estates that owed anything. A few hundred families covered more than two-thirds of the bill. 
 Story Continues Estates between $10 million and $20 million show the opposite pattern. That group filed the most returns and had the most estates owing tax, 1,002, but it paid just $1,611,039,000 combined. Those estates sit close to the exemption, so only a small piece of their value gets taxed. 
 Federal Reserve data for the second quarter of 2026 show the top 1% of households hold 32.5% of U.S. household net worth and 50.9% of corporate equities and mutual fund shares. Stock portfolios and business interests are what the biggest estates are built on. 
 Why Filing-Year Data Lag the Current Rules 
 The returns filed in 2024 cover people who died in earlier years, and each estate was measured against the exemption in effect when that person died. For comparison, IRS guidance set the filing threshold at $13,610,000 for a citizen who died in 2024. So the 2024 data actually overstate how many estates would owe tax under today's rules. 
 What the $15 Million Exemption Means Now 
 For deaths in 2026, the tax code now sets the basic exclusion amount at $15,000,000 per person. It's indexed for inflation after 2026 and has no sunset date, a change the IRS links to the One, Big, Beautiful Bill. The IRS says the figure rises to $15,480,000 for deaths in 2027. 
 A surviving spouse can also claim a late spouse's unused exclusion. That only works if the executor files an estate tax return and makes the election, which is why some estates file even when they owe nothing. With that election, a married couple can shield up to $30,000,000 in 2026. 
 State Death Taxes Kick In Far Sooner 
 Most families won't owe federal estate tax, but some states set the bar much lower. Massachusetts requires an estate tax return once the gross estate passes $2,000,000. Maryland imposes both an estate tax and an inheritance tax under state law. Pennsylvania taxes inheritances too. 24/7 Wall St. has covered the rules in Massachusetts, Maryland, Pennsylvania, and other states. 
 Inheritance Rules That Affect Typical Families 
 Step-up in basis matters far more for most heirs. Under federal law, inherited property generally takes a tax basis equal to its fair market value on the date of death. That means gains built up during the parent's lifetime usually aren't taxed when an heir sells. 
 Beneficiary designations decide who gets life insurance and retirement accounts, and they can override a will. That's why keeping them up to date counts for a lot (we put the whole cleanup checklist, beneficiary forms and account titling included, in a free estate guide). Inherited retirement accounts also carry income tax. For most non-spouse beneficiaries of owners who died after 2019, the SECURE Act requires the entire balance be distributed within ten years. Withdrawals from an inherited traditional IRA are generally taxed as income. 
 Federal estate tax is a concern for a few thousand very wealthy families a year, and with the exemption rising again in 2027, that group should stay small. For nearly everyone else, the one check worth making is whether the state where a parent lives, or owns property, has its own estate or inheritance tax.
